result.document_summary: Official text of California Civil Code section 1947.12, the statewide residential rent increase cap (5% plus CPI, max 10%) as amended by SB 567, operative April 1, 2024 and repealed January 1, 2030.
result.notes: Single rule extracted: the statewide rent cap. Coverage is modeled from the certificate-of-occupancy exemption (15 years) and the owner-occupied duplex exemption; other exemptions (affordable housing, dormitories, local rent control stricter than the cap, separately alienable property with non-corporate owner and notice) cannot be tested with available facts and are modeled as 'other' or owner_type facts. The section references Civ. Code 1946.2 only in an exemption notice statement, so no just-cause rule is extracted from this document. Section is repealed as of 2030-01-01 by its own terms.

rules.title: California statewide residential rent increase cap (Tenant Protection Act, as amended by SB 567)
rules.requirement: An owner of residential real property may not raise the gross rental rate more than 5 percent plus the local percentage change in cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period, and no more than two increments in that period. The owner may set the initial rent for a new tenancy in which no prior tenant remains.
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower
rules.coverage_text: Applies to residential rental dwellings and units in California (including mobilehome park units), except those exempted, notably housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years.

exemptions.label: New construction: certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (not mobilehome)

all_of.text: Housing that has been issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless the housing is a mobilehome.
A property containing two separate dwelling units within a single structure

the owner occupied one of the units as the owner's principal place of residence at the beginning of the tenancy, so long as the owner continues in occupancy, and neither unit is an accessory dwelling unit or a junior accessory dwelling unit

exemptions.label: Separately alienable property (e.g., single-family home or condo) with non-corporate owner and written exemption notice

all_of.value: natural person (not REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member)
all_of.text: The owner is not a real estate investment trust, a corporation, a limited liability company in which at least one member is a corporation, or management of a mobilehome park

all_of.value: alienable separate from title to any other dwelling unit and tenants given written exemption notice
all_of.text: Residential real property that is alienable separate from the title to any other dwelling unit, provided the tenants have been provided written notice that the property is exempt

Housing restricted by deed, regulatory restriction, or other recorded document as affordable housing for very low, low, or moderate income persons, or subject to an agreement providing housing subsidies

exemptions.label: Dormitories owned and operated by a higher education institution or K-12 school

all_of.text: Dormitories owned and operated by an institution of higher education or a kindergarten and grades 1 to 12, inclusive, school.

exemptions.label: Housing under local rent control that restricts annual increases to less than the state cap

all_of.value: subject to local rent or price control restricting annual increases below the state cap
all_of.text: Housing subject to rent or price control through a public entity's valid exercise of its police power consistent with Chapter 2.7 that restricts annual increases in the rental rate to an amount less than that provided in subdivision (a).
This section shall not apply to a homeowner of a mobilehome, as defined in Section 798.9.

rules.exemptions_text: Exempt: deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; school/college dormitories; housing under stricter local rent control; housing with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); separately alienable property whose owner is not a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member and where written exemption notice was given; owner-occupied duplexes; homeowners of mobilehomes.
rules.interaction: Does not apply to housing under a valid local rent control (Civ. Code ch. 2.7, § 1954.50 et seq.) that limits annual increases below the state cap; the section does not expand or limit local governments' authority to adopt rent controls consistent with that chapter. Cross-references Civ. Code § 1946.2 (just cause) in the exemption notice.
yields_to: Local rent or price control consistent with Cal. Civ. Code ch. 2.7 (§ 1954.50 et seq.) that restricts annual increases below the state cap
